newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Mosel limit up on ex-bonus issue.
newsitem.headline: Mosel limit up on ex-bonus issue.

text.p: Taiwan's chipmaker Mosel Vitelic Inc surged in early Tuesday trade on its ex-bonus issue date, and brokers saw more rises ahead.
Mosel issued a stock dividend, or bonus issue, of T$4 per share, paying 400 shares free for every 1,000 shares held.
After 55 minutes at 0155 GMT, Mosel was up by the daily seven percent limit to T$66.

"Mosel's surge follows a recent pattern that almost all electronics, especially chipmakers, would surge for some time after their ex-bonus issues, for the sector's expected sound outlook," said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin.
Several electronic shares had regained pre-bonus issue levels.
With Mosel's Monday closing price at T$87.5 before the bonus issue, Lin said Mosel had room to rise further.
In May, Mosel and Siliconware Precision announced they would invest a combined T$10 billion to form a joint-venture integrated circuits assembly and testing plant.
The assembly and testing plant would service Mosel's new US$1.7 billion chip-making venture with German electronics giant Siemens AG that is set to begin production in June.
